details: CONFIRMED by a probe. Before the change an absolute value was dead (joined as "<main>//abs"), so the guard stayed on; the
change makes it live with no check that the folder does not hold the main checkout. wt_root takes the first path component
under the extra folder as the worktree root, which for any path in main is main itself. relay_setup.gitignore_lines already
treats folders outside the project as a supported setting, and a sibling layout is the common alternative to nested
worktrees, so a person can reach this with one line of kit.toml; the result is a silent loss of the main-checkout guard
(edits and git commits on the default branch pass). No live kit.toml sets an absolute value today (queue item note), hence
evidence: git commit in main exit 2 guard-main: mutating git command in the main checkout: git commit (...)
failing_case: main checkout <tmp>/code/app, kit.toml [project] worktrees = "<tmp>/code" (worktrees beside the checkout, the layout
"git worktree add <tmp>/code/<name>" gives). Edit <tmp>/code/app/README.md, Edit <tmp>/code/app/lib/x.py, Bash
"git commit --allow-empty -m x" with cwd = main: all exit 0 now (wt_root returns "<tmp>/code/app" as a task worktree, so
in_main is False everywhere in main). On master all three exit 2. Expected: exit 2, the main checkout is never a task worktree.
fix_hint: In wt_root, after computing the root under the extra folder, return it only when it is not self.main and does not contain
main (root != self.main and not self.main.startswith(root + "/")); else fall through to the listed-worktree check. Add a test
with worktrees = the parent of main (pass cases 1 and 2).
pass_cases: 1. worktrees = "<tmp>/code" (parent of main <tmp>/code/app): Edit <tmp>/code/app/README.md -> exit 2; git commit in main -> exit 2.
2. Same setting: Edit <tmp>/code/feature/f.py (a sibling folder under the extra) -> exit 0.
3. worktrees = "<main>/wts" (absolute, under main): Edit <main>/wts/a/f.py -> exit 0 (the branch's new test).
findings.summary: an absolute project.worktrees that contains the main checkout (a sibling layout, worktrees = the parent folder) now switches the guard off for the whole main checkout

details: PLAUSIBLE (traced by reading; not run). main is os.path.realpath'd at load and every tool path goes through resolve()
(realpath of the nearest existing ancestor), but extra_dir() returns the configured absolute string as is. Correct for the
usual spelled-as-real path; fragile otherwise. Size: 5 minutes (os.path.realpath on the absolute value, or resolve(wtdir, main)).
evidence: guard_main.py:162-173 resolve() realpaths; :219 main realpath; :272 extra_dir returns self.wtdir unchanged when absolute.
failing_case: macOS, main /private/tmp/p (reached as /tmp/p), kit.toml worktrees = "/tmp/p/wts". Edit /tmp/p/wts/a/f.py: resolve() gives
/private/tmp/p/wts/a/f.py, extra_dir() is "/tmp/p/wts", no match, and with no git-registered worktree there the write is
refused as a write to main (exit 2). Expected exit 0, as with worktrees = "/private/tmp/p/wts".
fix_hint: extra_dir: return resolve(self.wtdir, self.main) when absolute (it also expands ~), else main + "/" + wtdir.
pass_cases: 1. worktrees = "<symlinked spelling of main>/wts": Edit <main>/wts/a/f.py -> exit 0.
2. worktrees = "<realpath of main>/wts": Edit <main>/wts/a/f.py -> exit 0 (the branch's new test).
